issues.title: Turbo rattle and underboost need wastegate linkage and pressure-side diagnosis
issues.cause: Factory may find loose actuator-rod clip, bypass diaphragm leakage or charge-air hose leak without internal turbo defect.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Check warm-exhaust safety; record T7 DTCs/actual pressure, visually inspect linkage, bypass diaphragm and correctly isolated charge-air plumbing with relevant year WIS.
issues.correction_summary: Repair confirmed linkage, hose or bypass valve first; reserve turbo replacement for independently demonstrated turbo failure.
limits: WIS loose clip result only search excerpt.
2005 pressure leak test is not automatically valid in 2007.

issues.title: Early 9-5 automatic can have repairable shift-control faults
issues.cause: Factory TSB 440-2497 differentiates software/TCM, sensor, servo and modified valve body causes from internal failure.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Map exact MY2002–04 symptom to TSB row, vehicle VIN/gearbox serial and TCM software, fluid, DTC, electrical and adaptation evidence.
issues.correction_summary: Follow specific TSB first-stage correction; replace complete transmission only when factory escalation, damage or persistent failure warrants it.
limits: Part 5449780 is a MY2002–03 candidate, not global retrofit.
Actual internal wear might still demand overhaul.

issues.title: CHECK GEARBOX electronic codes do not alone condemn 9-5 automatic
issues.cause: Saab DTC documentation includes P0748 pressure-control electrical current and P0722 missing output speed, with transmission limp-home.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Check code criteria, all systems and harness, match installed ATF inspection method; distinguish sensor electrical failures from actual gear slipping.
issues.correction_summary: Address confirmed circuit/fluid faults and retest. Rebuild only if physical internal damage or persistent factory-diagnosed fault.
limits: MY2006 P0730 has independent source-year and is not the same DTC.
No guarantee electrical repair cures internal damage.
Never disable safety interlocks for testing.

issues.title: Overheating: differentiate external cooling faults from proven engine damage
issues.cause: Factory specifies separate thermostat, coolant cap and gauge thresholds plus thermostat housing grounds and seals.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Shut down an overheating engine. When cold, inspect leaks, coolant quality and thermometer/scan data; perform professional system pressure or combustion-gas test if supported.
issues.correction_summary: Replace only confirmed external faulty part; if head warp, oil contamination, low compression or persistent blow-by is verified, evaluate major engine repair.
limits: Factory nominal temperatures do not identify head-gasket failure.
No proven non-invasive test guarantees engine health.
Do not run an overheated engine for a diagnostic drive.
